target.title: fix(group): keep group id display truncation UTF-16 safe
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where the human-readable group session label could show a broken surrogate character when the truncation boundary at 6 characters fell inside an emoji or other surrogate-pair character.

## Why This Change Was Made

The `shortenGroupId` function truncates chat group labels for display using raw `String.prototype.slice()`, which does not account for UTF-16 surrogate pairs. Replacing with `truncateUtf16Safe` ensures that multi-code-unit characters are kept intact or dropped entirely.

## User Impact

Group session display labels in TUI and diagnostics remain well-formed when the group name contains emoji or CJK characters.

## Evidence

- Uses the same `truncateUtf16Safe` helper already used in 100+ files across the codebase.
- The call chain ensures truncation happens before the label is shown to the operator, so the fix directly prevents broken renderings.
- `shortenGroupId` is now exported and tested directly via the production function path (previously the test had a duplicated local copy).

## Test Evidence

\`\`\`
$ npx vitest run src/config/sessions/group.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
 Tests  12 passed (12)
\`\`\`

All 12 tests pass, including the UTF-16 safety tests that exercise the real `shortenGroupId` function exported from `src/config/sessions/group.ts`.

## Runtime Evidence

The actual `shortenGroupId` function called with realistic inputs:

| Input | Output | Notes |
|-------|--------|-------|
| \`abcdefghijklmnop\` (16 chars) | \`abcdef...mnop\` | ASCII, correct truncation |
| \`abcdefghij😱klm\` (14 chars + emoji) | \`abcdef...😱klm\` | Emoji at suffix boundary preserved intact |
| \`0123456789xy😱ab\` (14 chars + emoji) | \`012345...y😱ab\` | All 4 code points in suffix including emoji |
| \`😱\` x 10 | \`😱😱😱...😱😱😱😱\` | Multiple emoji, no orphaned surrogates |
| \`short\` | \`short\` | Short strings unchanged |
| \`\` (empty) | \`\` | Empty returns empty string |

Key behavioral proof: Input \`abcdefghij😱klm\` — the emoji 😱 (U+1F631) is a surrogate pair at UTF-16 positions 10-11. The old \`trimmed.slice(-4)\` would start at position 11 (the low surrogate), producing an orphaned \`\\ude31\` in the output. The fix with \`truncateUtf16Safe\` and \`[...trimmed].slice(-4)\` (code-point-aware) keeps the emoji intact.

The test refactor (exporting \`shortenGroupId\` instead of keeping a local copy in the test file) ensures the tests exercise the actual production code path, preventing future drift between the implementation and its tests.

**What was not tested**:
- Integration with real chat channels (Signal, Telegram, Matrix, etc.) — relies on unit-level correctness of \`truncateUtf16Safe\` which is already proven at the util layer
- Browser/Electron UI rendering — the fix is at the data transformation layer; any UI rendering is a separate concern
